items.text: Oil rallied sharply post-UAE/Iran conflict escalation, with WTI down -2% from 86.04 to 84.25 but remaining structurally elevated vs. pre-shock levels. Energy shock is re-intensifying: July 7 US strikes triggered gas price spikes and reversal of early-month sentiment gains. For credit investors, sustained oil >$80–85 keeps refinancing costs elevated for energy debt and amplifies refiners' hedging costs; CCC spreads at 1005bp reflect this risk premia.

June payrolls collapsed to just 57K vs. 129K prior (data through 2026-06), a dramatic deceleration. Claims remain historically low at 187K as of 7/18, but job growth has stalled. With unemployment at 4.2% and wage growth easing to 3.52% YoY, the labor market is cooling but not cracking. For special situations: slower job growth reduces corporate pricing power and increases refinancing pressure; look for credit stress in leveraged names that depend on wage growth or tight labor tailwinds.

Headline CPI cooled to 3.46% (vs. 4.17%) by June, and core eased to 2.57% (vs. 2.82%), providing some relief. However, PCE remains sticky at 4.07% headline and 3.41% core as of May data, above Fed's target. Oil shock adds upside risk to 2H26 CPI. For credit: moderating headline inflation weakens near-term refinancing argument, but sticky core and renewed energy shock keep real yields elevated and refinancing spreads volatile.

Fed paused at 3.75%; market prices ~89% no-change next meeting, and June projections showed no cuts expected in 2026. ECB raised 25bp in June to 2.25% and held in late July, citing energy shocks; Lagarde flagged September as likely for next move. Peak rates are in place and hiking risk has re-emerged. For credit: no near-term rate relief; 10Y curve has steepened to 45bp (from 34bp), reflecting growth weakness vs. inflation fears; call spreads are widening, pressuring refinancing windows.

HY OAS widened to 284bp (+7bp) and CCC OAS jumped to 1005bp (+14bp), signaling rising stress at the bottom. IG slightly wider at 81bp (+2bp). VIX ticked to 18.21 (+116bp) on geopolitical unease. Steepening curve and widening spreads suggest credit rotation lower as growth slows and refinancing risk rises. Special situations investors should monitor Q3 earnings for CFO guidance on debt maturity profiles and refinancing intentions; covenant-lite and unsecured names face real pressure in this regime.

Retail sales stalled in June at +0.2% MoM (vs. +1.0% in May), core sales turned negative, and momentum is fading. However, UMich sentiment rebounded sharply to 54.4 in July prelim (vs. 49.5 June and 44.8 May) on falling gas prices—though 70%+ of interviews predated the July 7 escalation and subsequent gas spike. Housing starts surged to 1427K but existing home sales fell 2.4% YoY, signaling mixed demand. For credit: consumer is slowing after 2H25 strength; housing weakness pressures construction and related credit; upbeat sentiment may not persist if energy prices remain elevated.

Q1 2026 GDP came in at 2.1% (vs. 0.5% prior), but recent soft data—weak payrolls, slowing retail, narrowing PMIs—suggest deceleration toward 1.5–2.0% range in H2. GDPNow at 1.54% as of April. China's official PMI at 50.3 in June shows modest expansion but fragility amid weak domestic demand. For special situations: sub-2% growth increasingly likely, which compresses leverage multiples and pressures defensive credit; watch for earnings misses and covenant stress tests, particularly in cyclicals and consumer-exposed credits.

themeCards.title: Middle East Oil Shock Redux
themeCards.statusLine: US Iran strikes resumed July 7; gas prices spiked, reversing early-month sentiment gains and raising 2H26 CPI risk. Oil structural floor now ~$80–85 vs. pre-conflict baseline of $65–70.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-sensitive credits (refiners, upstream, plastics/chemical) face margin compression and refinancing risk; spillover to inflation psychology could trigger Fed rate-path repricing and widen credit curves.

themeCards.title: Manufacturing PMI Softening into Q3
themeCards.statusLine: ISM Mfg fell to 53.3 in June (from 54.0); employment still in contraction (49.7). China's factory PMI barely above 50. Early signs of Q3 momentum loss.
themeCards.relevance: Cyclical credit—autos, capital equipment, industrials—faces demand headwinds; watch for earnings downgrades and refinancing wall stress, especially in leveraged buyouts in these sectors.

themeCards.title: Payroll Cliff & Labor Market Divergence
themeCards.statusLine: June payrolls collapsed to 57K (vs. 129K prior), starkest monthly drop in years. Claims remain low, but job creation has essentially stopped. Possible seasonal adjustment error or genuine demand destruction.
themeCards.relevance: If sustained, signals recession risk and erodes debt service capacity across consumer-sensitive credits; refinancing risk for firms dependent on wage inflation tailwinds intensifies.

themeCards.title: Refinancing Wall & Spread Widening Concurrence
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS 284bp, CCC 1005bp, curve flattening (10Y-2Y = 45bp). No Fed rate cuts priced for 2026; peak-rate environment persists. Maturity walls in H2 2026/H1 2027 face higher rollover costs.
themeCards.relevance: Leveraged finance, especially mezzanine and covenant-lite structures, faces real refinancing stress. Special situations should target names with tight maturities, weak FCF generation, or deteriorating asset quality.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Fragility
themeCards.statusLine: UMich sentiment jumped to 54.4 in July prelim on gas price declines, but survey 70%+ pre-escalation. Retail sales momentum faded (0.2% MoM June vs. 1.0% prior); sentiment likely to reverse if energy re-spikes.
themeCards.relevance: Consumer credit and retail-linked debt beneficiaries of recent sentiment relief may face rapid repricing if energy shock persists. High credit card utilization and auto loan stress already building; watch for delinquency uptick.

themeCards.title: China Demand Weakness & Property Risk Spillover
themeCards.statusLine: China PMI shows narrow expansion (50.3) with weak new orders and job losses. Domestic demand remains subdued despite AI-led export strength. Property sector weakness ongoing.
themeCards.relevance: US firms with China supply-chain or end-market exposure face earnings headwinds; emerging-market credit linked to China commodities or financing faces credit compression. Watch for China bank stress signals.

regime.label: Late-cycle slowdown with inflation persistence
regime.detail: Payroll cliff, fading retail momentum, and manufacturing deceleration signal demand erosion. Fed paused, peak rates entrenched. Oil shock re-intensifying. Spreads widening, refinancing stress rising. Growth sub-2% ahead.
